title: The will for a will: Adam Kadmon as the true creation from nothing
overview:
The chapter goes one step below the *ratzon kadum*. That preceding will, for Himself, is a will for the end of the deed; out of it comes a *ratzon l'ratzon*, a will for a will: the will to have any will needed to get the final thing. Will for *Atzilus*, will for *Beriya* like an architect, will for *Asiya*, and even for the dirt and the noise of the building site. These ten wills for a will are the ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon*, the hidden root of the revealed *sefiros* of *Atzilus*.

*Adam Kadmon* is the Man of *Beriya* because a will for a will is created *yesh me'ayin* and stays a nothing: when the buddy shows up with the pizza, the will to find the keys is gone without a trace, as the world would be if the *Aibershter* took His mind off it. *Adam Kadmon* is the *ma'atzil*; *Atzilus* only reveals it. Above it is the *ratzon kadum* itself, still thinking only of itself, of sitting and not of a chair: the *Rambam*'s "knowledge of Himself". No class reads the chapter's first fourteen lines; after a jump in the tape, only his explanation of lines 13-14 is heard.

sections.title: The Keser of Adam Kadmon is the true creation from nothing
sections.summary: The last level of the *ratzon kadum* becomes the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, which is called a creation *yesh me'ayin*, the true one, because the *ratzon kadum* is the *hiyuli* source of every will for a will. The series has no class on these lines.

sections.title: An example from the soul: the will for a will is a new creation
sections.summary: When the essential desire for kindness in the *yechida* turns to one thing, it is first a hidden will still for itself; when it dresses itself in the intellect and thought of that thing, it is a new creation, called *Beriya*. No class reads these lines; after a jump in the tape, his explanation of the last two is heard.

phrases.he: שהרי אנו רואים שלא בכל העתים יהיה לאדם רצון לרצון פרטי,
שבהכרח יש מקור המהווה לרצון זה הפרטי ונקרא רצון לרצון זה,

blocks.text: Sometimes he wants *mischar* (trade), sometimes not: his will for himself makes a will for a will for whatever he needs.

blocks.text: So the *ratzon kadum* is no *beriya chadasha* (new creation) but always there, part of the true *ayin*: not a nothing, but not a something by itself.

sections.title: Not always there: the source of the will for a will also comes from nothing, like a bribe
sections.summary: The will for a will comes and goes and shines strongly or weakly, so its source too comes into being something from nothing. A bribe shows it: it reaches the essence of the soul, and from it a will to acquit is always drawn.

phrases.he: וממילא מובן מאחר שלא בכל העתים נמשך הרצון לרצון זה,
וגם לפעמים יאיר אור רב ותקיף
נמצא מוכרח שגם המקור העושה ומהוה לרצון זה,
הוא גם כן בא בבחינת התהוות יש מאין

phrases.en: Like a bribe.

phrases.he: שיעשה רצון לרצון ושכל לזכות תמיד
שמחמתו יומשך תמיד התהוות רצון לרצון של חסד וזכות
ולהיפך לשונאו יתהווה תמיד רצון לרצון של דין כו'

blocks.text: One remark on lines 15-18: **Like a bribe**, which reaches the soul's essence, so a will to acquit keeps coming, and toward an enemy, a will to condemn.

sections.title: Ten wills for a will: the ten sefiros of Adam Kadmon, hidden source of Atzilus
sections.summary: Every revealed will has ten, so there are ten wills for a will: the ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon*, wills for whatever the *dira b'tachtonim* needs, dirt included. They are the hidden root of the revealed *sefiros* of *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: וידוע דכל רצון גלוי כלול מי'.
phrases.en: So we see that any *ratzon galui* is made up of ten.
So we must say,

phrases.he: גם הרצון לרצון זה כלול מי'
ממילא יש י' מיני רצון לרצון,
שמתהווים כולם בבחינת יש מאין כו'
phrases.en: and all of them come in a way of *yesh me'ayin*.

blocks.text: Every revealed will is made of ten, so this will for a will has ten kinds, and **all of them come in a way of *yesh me'ayin***.

phrases.he: וכל זה דוגמא להבין בבחינת עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון,
phrases.en: This is all a *mashal* on the ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.text: **This is all a *mashal* on the ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon***: wanting a *dira b'tachtonim* (dwelling below), He willed whatever it needs, first *Atzilus*: what He wants in that dwelling.
Then *Beriya*, a concept, as an architect makes; *Yetzira*, the form; down to *Asiya*, the actual building. That includes things opposite to the will but needed for it, "like a bunch of dirt."

blocks.title: The wife at the building site
blocks.text: A man takes his wife to the house he is building, and she's very happy. Another lady asks why: "I thought you hate dirt. Look, a bunch of dirty guys, lowlifes, trash-type people, building your house with cigarettes in their mouth, and you hate cigarettes. They're cursing, banging hammers, dust all over: *mamash* the opposite of what you want. This is what your husband gives you, and instead of shouting at him you're happy?" "Yes, because that's how I'll get the final thing." So too the *Aibershter* made all kinds of things, *mamash* lowlifes.

sensitivity.reason: Builders on a site are called dirty guys, lowlifes and trash-type people.

blocks.text: The whole world is full of lowlifes.

sensitivity.reason: A blunt remark that the world is full of lowlifes.

blocks.text: "He saw it is very good": it gets Him the final thing, even the *yetzer hara* (evil inclination), which seems its opposite.
A will for a will is whatever the final thing needs: ten powers, ten such wills, all *yesh me'ayin*, the ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon*.

phrases.en: That's the *helem*,

blocks.text: **That's the *helem***: *Adam Kadmon* is new, something from nothing; *Atzilus*, as will be learned, only reveals what is already in it.

phrases.en: the *ratzon* of *chachma*,
that's where it's rooted,

phrases.he: וכן כתר שבחסד דאצילות מכתר שבחסד דאדם קדמון כו'

blocks.text: *Keser* of *chachma* of *Atzilus*, the will in the intellect, is rooted in that of *Adam Kadmon*, the will for a will for *chachma*; so too *chesed* and the rest.

sections.title: From the Kav: the last level of the ratzon kadum becomes Keser of Adam Kadmon
sections.summary: The ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* come from the *Kav*, here the *ratzon kadum* itself. Its *Malchus*, the ambition to have the thing in deed, becomes *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*: the will to have any will needed. *Adam Kadmon* is the *ma'atzil*, and *Atzilus* only reveals it.

phrases.he: ואמנם התהוות עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון עצמו,
שנקרא מקור התהוות כל הרצונות לרצונות כו'

phrases.en: Since the *ratzon kadum* is really the actual *etzem haratzon* of the *ratzon hapashut*,
that it should be like this, like we explained before.

blocks.text: The ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* come from the *Kav*, here the *ratzon kadum*, **the actual *etzem haratzon* of the *ratzon hapashut***, which from the first was that it should be so.

phrases.he: על כן הוא פועל ועושה רצון לרצון בדרך פרט
והוא מבחינת כתר דאדם קדמון עד בחינת מלכות שבו,
שהוא בחינת רצון לרצון דמלוכה כו'

blocks.text: So it makes a will for a will in particular, from *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* to its *Malchus*: to actually make the house.

phrases.he: ואמנם רק מבחינת אחרונה שברצון הקדום ההיולי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: But in particular it's only from *Malchus* of the *ratzon kadum*
becomes *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*.
means the *ratzon* for the *ratzon l'ratzon*,

phrases.he: שלמעלה מחכמה שברצון לרצון הנעלם כו'
phrases.en: and that's higher than the *chachma* of *Adam Kadmon*, means *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.text: In particular, *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, the hidden will for a will, above its *chachma*, comes only from *Malchus* of the *ratzon kadum*: the last circle, for an actual deed.
The daydream ends in doing the thing; from that inner ambition, *Malchus* of the *ratzon kadum*, comes the *Keser*: a will for any will he might need.

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה כל עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון, הכל בבחינת ההעלם
ורצון לרצון לכל עשר ספירות דאצילות שבא בבחינת גלוי,

phrases.en: And this will be explained later.

blocks.text: So all of *Adam Kadmon* is a hidden will for a will for *Atzilus*, which, as will be explained, is only *Adam Kadmon* revealed.

*Adam Kadmon* is new. Many think the *ma'atzil* (emanator) is His Essence; it is *Adam Kadmon*, and *Atzilus* is *ne'etzal* (emanated) from it. Where *Atzilus* is said to come from the *Atzmus*, it means *Adam Kadmon*, still counted part of the *etzem*.

sections.title: Like the pizza: a will for a will vanishes as if it never was
sections.summary: *Adam Kadmon* is the Man of *Beriya* because a will for a will is created from nothing, and stays nothing: when the reason for it goes, it is gone without a trace, as the world would be if the *Aibershter* took His mind off it.

phrases.he: וזהו שבחינת אדם קדמון נקרא אדם דבריאה כו',

phrases.en: is *mamash* something from nothing,

phrases.he: שהתהוות הרצון לרצון לעתים מיוחדים הוא בא,

phrases.en: like something comes into being from nothing.

blocks.text: So *Adam Kadmon* is the Man of *Beriya*: it **is *mamash* something from nothing**, like a will for a will.

blocks.title: The buddy who brought a pizza
blocks.text: He wants a pizza, and at once there is a will for a will to find his keys and wallet and take the car. Then his buddy knocks with a pizza and the football game. Will he refuse, wanting to go out in his car? That will, *yesh me'ayin*, vanishes as if it never was.

blocks.question: Why would the world cease to exist if the *Aibershter* took His mind off it for a second?
blocks.text: Nobody would have to destroy the world; it would cease to exist *lechatchila* (from the outset), like those wills for a will.

blocks.title: The pizza: no avoda needed to drop it
blocks.text: No *avoda* (inner work) is needed to drop the will to drive to the pizza store; it vanishes without a *reshimu* (impression): "Hey, my buddy is here with a pizza."
Once created it is still *yesh me'ayin*, with no existence of its own: when its cause goes, wanted no more or attained, it's gone. So with all *ABYA*, the angels, everything: "It's all incidental."

sections.title: Where a will for a will first appears: thought, the hidden thought of Adam Kadmon
sections.summary: Thought is the vessel of the will, so a will for a will first comes into being in thought, the will in thought. That is *Keser*, *chachma* and *bina* of *Adam Kadmon*: the action of the will for a will in the *machshava stima'a* of *Adam Kadmon*.

phrases.en: like when a thought comes up from a *midda*,

phrases.he: שהיא התהוות יש מאין לגבי עצמיות הרצון שבנפשו
כנראה בחוש שהרצון לרצון הבא בבחינת התהוות כנזכר לעיל,

phrases.en: in general, any *ratzon* is *mis'haveh* in a *machshava*.

blocks.text: Like thought coming from a *midda* (attribute), *yesh me'ayin* to the will's essence, a will for a will begins in thought; **in general, any *ratzon* is *mis'haveh* in a *machshava***.

phrases.en: it says that Haman thought to do, meant he wanted to do.

phrases.he: וכן תחלת התהוות רצון לרצון במחשבה,

phrases.en: this *ratzon* of a *machshava*.

blocks.text: Thought is the will's *kli* (vessel): to want, you think, "I want that pizza." Haman "thought to do": he wanted to.
So a will for a will begins as will in thought. Later: two kinds of thought, of the will and of *iyun* (analysis).

phrases.he: וזהו כללות ענין כח''ב דאדם קדמון
phrases.en: which means the *machshava* of *Adam Kadmon*,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת התהוות פעולת אור רצון לרצון דרך פרט

phrases.en: means *machshava stima'a* of *Adam Kadmon*, not *machshava stima'a* of *Arich*.

blocks.text: *Keser*, *chachma* and *bina* of *Adam Kadmon* are the will for a will acting in its *machshava stima'a* (hidden thought), not *Arich*'s: its total hiddenness.

sections.title: Above it, the Kav itself: thinking only of himself, like the Rambam's self-knowledge
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* is above even the hidden thought of *Adam Kadmon*: it still thinks only to itself all that will be, sitting and not yet a chair. That is what the *Rambam* calls "His knowledge of Himself", which is the *machshava kduma* and not the *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בבחינת הקו עצמו
שלמעלה מבחינת פעולת התהוות רצון לרצון לדבר פרט במחשבה סתימאה גם כן כו'
רק לעצמו עדיין חושב כל מה שיהיה כו'
phrases.en: He is still really thinking to himself,
that it includes really what he's thinking about himself,

phrases.he: ולא בהתהוות רצון במחשבה שחוץ ממנו כלל
phrases.en: It's not a *ratzon* in the *machshava* which is outside of him yet.

blocks.text: Not so the *Kav* itself, *stima d'chol stimin* (most hidden of all). Here he means the *ratzon kadum*, still thinking of itself, "not about the pizza yet."

blocks.title: Sell the sizzle, not the steak
blocks.text: Salesmen are told, "you sell the sizzle and not the steak": a good salesman reaches the *ratzon kadum*, the will for himself.
**He is still really thinking to himself**: of sitting, not a chair. Sitting includes a will for a will to buy one, but no will yet in a thought outside him.
The *Rambam*'s "His knowledge of Himself" many take for the *Atzmus*; it is the *hiyuli* of thought, the *machshava kduma*. End of chapter.

reviewQuestions.question: Why is *Adam Kadmon* a new creation, something from nothing, while *Atzilus* is not?
What does the wife at the building site show about the wills for a will that make up *Adam Kadmon*?
From which level of the *ratzon kadum* does *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* come, and what is it a will for?
Who is the *ma'atzil*, and what does it mean when someone reads that *Atzilus* comes from the *Atzmus*?
What happens to the will to drive to the pizza store when the buddy shows up, and what does that say about the world?
How is the *Kav* itself different from the hidden thought of *Adam Kadmon*, and what is the *Rambam*'s "knowledge of Himself"?

notes.text: No class reads lines 1-14. Class 027 ends chapter 17 with "And that was chapter 17" (w814-818); the recording then jumps from 6:20 to 6:30 and resumes in the middle of his explanation of lines 13-14 (w819-969: "sometimes he wants mischar and sometimes he doesn't", the will for a will, and the ratzon kadum that is not a new creation), then reads from the second half of line 15 ("it follows of necessity", w970). The jump probably cut the reading of lines 1-14 and the start of his explanation. Their phrases therefore have no English: lines 13-14 keep Hebrew-only phrases because the passage carries his explanation, and the first half of line 15 is never read. The pizza and the architect he refers back to in lines 34-35 and 21 come from chapter 16's classes. chapter_17.json also cites w819-969, under its last passage, as a remark on that chapter.

Lines 15-20 and 41-43 are read with no translation of their own; their phrases carry his wording only where he gives any ("so we must say", "they all of them come in a way of yesh me'ayin") and otherwise have no English.

Class 028 w42-85: part of the sentence on the ratzon hapashut is garbled ("that originally was negly pleev"); the block renders it from the line's own words, "which from the first was that it should be like this".
For line 38's "and he thought to do" he cites Haman ("it says that Haman thought to do, meant he wanted to do"); left as he said it.
For line 40's "Kachab" he reads "Keser Chabad", and renders the phrase "which means the machshava of Adam Kadmon" (028 w1107-1112).

The building-site mashal is flagged other-groups for calling the builders lowlifes and trash-type people, and "the whole world is full of lowlifes" (w1504-1510) is an aside of its own, flagged the same way; both publishable texts keep the teaching (the opposite things are what get the final thing).
028 w1278-1336, after the phone call: he goes back over lines 38 and 41-42, partly in Yiddish; the transcript is garbled, so it is listed as unclear.
